examples.title: Do not start because a checklist box was ticked
examples.situation: The source's first five bank boxes are ticked, but engine oil was not checked and the training machine differs from the example.
reasoning: Stop; identify the actual device/manual and perform its complete checks, including oil, leaks, guards and controls.
Do not trust a planted loose bolt or start with an unknown fault.
Reassess operator eligibility and site; an ineligible learner studies an inert example.
examples.takeaway: No start and no practical pass until the gate is satisfied.

examples.title: One learner, one safe pass
examples.situation: An eligible learner has an approved cleared row, but a person enters the turning area at 20 m.
reasoning: Disengage/stop according to the actual manual immediately and prevent tine contact.
Record the interrupted distance and reason; do not let a second person grab moving handlebars.
Resume only after the trainer restores the clear-area gate and the learner is ready.
examples.takeaway: Safety and crop preservation outrank finishing the 30 m distance.

examples.title: Timebox without removing safety
examples.situation: The source table says 35 minutes of work plus 10 discussion, but four activity phases sum to 40 minutes.
reasoning: Keep briefing, inspection/start, pass/evaluation and stop/clean as distinct outputs.
The trainer schedules adequate individual turns and discussion rather than pretending all learners passed in 35 minutes.
An unperformed phase remains pending and is recorded.
examples.takeaway: A flexible realistic schedule with no skipped safety-critical action.
